nodes.summary: For a history with `K ≥ 1` pieces and `m ≥ 2`, writing `a = C(m,2)` and `R = cumRate h.sizeFn`, `a c_m = size 0 + ∑_{j=1}^{K-1} (size j - size (j-1)) exp(-a R(start j))`. In particular the integral defining `c_m` converges.
nodes.title: Closed form of the first-coalescence times

nodes.summary: The dual cumulative rate inverts the cumulative rate.
nodes.title: Dual cumulative rate inverts the cumulative rate

nodes.summary: On piece `j` (including its right end), `1 / sizeFn` is integrable on `[0, s]` and the cumulative rate is affine: `R(s) = R(start j) + (s - start j) / size j`.
nodes.title: Cumulative rate is affine on each piece

nodes.summary: The coalescent-time breakpoints `R(start j)` are strictly increasing.
nodes.title: Coalescent-time breakpoints are strictly increasing

nodes.summary: The cumulative rate is strictly increasing on `[0, ∞)`.
nodes.title: Cumulative rate is strictly increasing

nodes.summary: The cumulative coalescence intensity `R(s) = ∫_0^s 1/η` of a relative population-size function `η` (pairs coalesce at rate `1/η(s)` at time `s` before the present). Meaningful for positive `η` with `1/η` locally integrable.
nodes.title: Cumulative coalescence intensity

nodes.summary: The dual history in coalescent time: piece `j` starts at `R(start j)` and has size `1 / size j`.
nodes.title: Dual history in coalescent time

nodes.summary: If two vectors of mean holding times give the same expected SFS for some `θ ≠ 0`, they agree at every `k = 2, …, n`. This is a direct consequence of `sfsKernel_eq_zero_of_lt` and `sfsKernel_diag_pos` (the kernel is triangular with nonzero diagonal); it is recorded here as an observation, not as a cited theorem.
nodes.title: The expected SFS determines the mean holding times

nodes.summary: On `[0, ∞)` the size function lies between the smallest and the largest piece size.
nodes.title: Size function lies between the extreme piece sizes

nodes.summary: For every `n` there are two measurable population-size functions, bounded between positive constants and different on a set of positive measure in `[0, ∞)`, with the same `c_m` for `2 ≤ m ≤ n` (two `(n + 2)`-piece histories from `PiecewiseHistory.exists_ne_firstCoalMean_eq_of_lt`, extended to `s < 0` by their size at `0`). This is the finite-sample shape of the statement of Myers, Fefferman & Patterson (2008);…
nodes.title: Non-identifiability from a bounded sample size

nodes.summary: Non-identifiability of general histories (Myers, Fefferman & Patterson 2008): there are two measurable population-size functions, bounded between positive constants, that differ on a set of positive Lebesgue measure in `[0, ∞)` and have the same expected first-coalescence time `c_m` for every `m ≥ 2` (hence the same expected SFS for every sample size).
nodes.title: Non-identifiability of general histories

nodes.summary: Tightness of `n ≥ 2K` (Bhaskar & Song 2014, Corollary 7): for every `K ≥ 2` there are two piecewise-constant histories with `K` pieces whose sizes differ at some time `s ≥ 0` but whose first-coalescence times `c_m` agree for `2 ≤ m ≤ 2K - 1`; so `sizeFn_eq_of_firstCoalMean_eq` fails for `n = 2K - 1`. The construction is explicit: with `z = 2^{-C(m,2)}`, the two histories have coalescent-time breakpoints…
nodes.title: Tightness of `n ≥ 2K`

nodes.summary: The two-piece case of `exists_ne_firstCoalMean_eq_of_lt`.
nodes.title: Distinct two-piece histories with equal first-coalescence times

nodes.summary: Every time `s ≥ 0` lies in some piece.
nodes.title: Every nonnegative time lies in some piece

nodes.summary: The size function is constant on an interval to the right of every `s ≥ 0`.
nodes.title: Size function is locally constant to the right

nodes.summary: Fay & Wu's `H = θ_π - θ_H` (Fay & Wu 2000).
nodes.title: Fay and Wu's H statistic

nodes.summary: Only the values on `[0, ∞)` enter the first-coalescence times.
nodes.title: First-coalescence times depend only on sizes at nonnegative times

nodes.summary: The expected time to the first coalescence among `m` lineages, `c_m = ∫_0^∞ exp(-C(m,2) R(s)) ds`, in a population of relative size `η` (Bhaskar & Song's `E[T_{m,m}]`). When the integrand is not integrable (for example `η ≡ 0`), this is Lean's junk value `0`; for piecewise-constant histories it is integrable (`choose_two_mul_firstCoalMean`).
nodes.title: Expected time to the first coalescence

nodes.summary: The numerator `S - a₁ ξ₁` of Fu & Li's `D` with an outgroup, where `S = ∑_i ξ_i` and the external-branch mutations are the derived singletons `ξ₁` (Fu & Li 1993).
nodes.title: Numerator of Fu and Li's D

nodes.summary: The numerator `θ_π - ξ₁` of Fu & Li's `F` with an outgroup (Fu & Li 1993), with `θ_π` in its SFS form.
nodes.title: Numerator of Fu and Li's F

nodes.summary: Fay & Wu's `H` has mean zero under the constant-size spectrum (`n ≥ 2`).
nodes.title: Fay and Wu's H has mean zero at constant size

nodes.summary: The numerator of Fu & Li's `D` has mean zero under the constant-size spectrum (`n ≥ 2`).
nodes.title: Numerator of Fu and Li's D has mean zero at constant size

nodes.summary: The numerator of Fu & Li's `F` has mean zero under the constant-size spectrum (`n ≥ 2`).
nodes.title: Numerator of Fu and Li's F has mean zero at constant size

nodes.summary: Expected SFS under a variable population size (Griffiths & Tavaré 1998; Polanski & Kimmel 2003). Let the genealogy of a sample of `n` copies consist of holding times `T k` (integrable for `2 ≤ k ≤ n`, otherwise arbitrary) and an independent block-size history `τ` with the random-joining law. If, given the genealogy, the count `ξ i` is integrable with conditional mean `(θ / 2) L_i`, then…
nodes.title: Expected SFS under a variable population size

nodes.summary: Achaz's unbiasedness under Kingman's coalescent, with the hypotheses of `SiteFrequencySpectrum.integral_sfs`.
nodes.title: Achaz's estimator is unbiased under Kingman's coalescent

nodes.summary: Achaz's unbiasedness (Achaz 2009): if `E ξ_i = θ / i` for `1 ≤ i ≤ n - 1` (the constant-size spectrum, `SiteFrequencySpectrum.integral_sfs`), every weighted estimator with `∑_i ω_i = 1` has mean `θ`.
nodes.title: Achaz's unbiasedness

nodes.summary: The size function is measurable.
nodes.title: Measurability of the piecewise size function

nodes.summary: A piecewise-constant population-size history with `K` pieces: piece `j < K` starts at time `start j` (backward from the present, `start 0 = 0`, strictly increasing) and has relative size `size j > 0`; the last piece extends to infinity. Adjacent pieces may have equal sizes, so this also covers histories with fewer than `K` distinct pieces. Values at indices `j ≥ K` are unused. The case `K = 0` is degenerate (its…
nodes.title: Piecewise-constant population-size history

nodes.summary: The kernel entry at `k = n - i + 1` is `(n - i + 1) / C(n-1, i-1) > 0`.
nodes.title: Positivity of the Griffiths–Tavaré kernel on the diagonal

nodes.summary: The kernel row `i` vanishes beyond `k = n - i + 1`: a branch subtending `i` copies cannot exist while more than `n - i + 1` lineages remain.
nodes.title: Griffiths–Tavaré kernel vanishes beyond the diagonal

nodes.summary: The Griffiths–Tavaré kernel `k C(n-i-1, k-2) / C(n-1, k-1)`: the expected number of branches subtending exactly `i` of the `n` sample copies while `k` lineages remain (`SiteFrequencySpectrum.joinStep_iterate_count`). Meaningful for `1 ≤ i < n`, `2 ≤ k ≤ n`; outside that range the natural-number subtractions give junk values.
nodes.title: Griffiths–Tavaré kernel

nodes.summary: The size at time `s` is the inverse of the dual history's size at coalescent time `R(s)`.
nodes.title: Size function is the inverse of the dual size in coalescent time

nodes.summary: Bhaskar–Song identifiability (Bhaskar & Song 2014, Corollary 7, "determined" half, stated for the first-coalescence times): two piecewise-constant histories with `K` pieces whose expected first-coalescence times `c_m` agree for `2 ≤ m ≤ n`, with `n ≥ 2K`, have the same population size at every time `s ≥ 0`. The proof writes `C(m,2) c_m` as an exponential sum in `C(m,2)` over at most `2K - 1` rates…
nodes.title: Bhaskar–Song identifiability

nodes.summary: On piece `j` the size function equals `size j`.
nodes.title: Size function on a piece equals the piece size

nodes.summary: The size function is positive on `[0, ∞)`.
nodes.title: Positivity of the piecewise size function

nodes.summary: The population-size function of a piecewise-constant history: at time `s ≥ 0` it is the size of the piece `j` with `start j ≤ s < start (j + 1)` (the last piece has no end). Equal to `0` for `s < 0` (junk; only `s ≥ 0` is meaningful).
nodes.title: Size function of a piecewise-constant history

nodes.summary: The start times are monotone on the pieces.
nodes.title: Monotonicity of piece start times

nodes.summary: Every piece starts at a nonnegative time.
nodes.title: Nonnegativity of piece start times

nodes.summary: Fay & Wu's `θ_H = ∑_i i² ξ_i / C(n,2)` (weights `i / C(n,2)`).
nodes.title: Fay and Wu's $\theta_H$

nodes.summary: Tajima's `θ_π` in its SFS form `∑_i i (n - i) ξ_i / C(n,2)` (weights `(n - i) / C(n,2)`).
nodes.title: Tajima's $\theta_\pi$ in site frequency spectrum form

nodes.summary: Achaz's weighted estimator `θ_ω = ∑_{i=1}^{n-1} ω_i i ξ_i` (Achaz 2009, with the weights already normalized).
nodes.title: Achaz's weighted estimator of $\theta$

nodes.summary: With the constant-size means `E T_k = 1 / C(k,2)`, the variable-size SFS is Fu's `θ / i`.
nodes.title: Variable-size spectrum reduces to Fu's $\theta/i$ at constant size

nodes.summary: The expected SFS entry `(θ / 2) ∑_{k=2}^{n} sfsKernel n i k · t k` of a sample of size `n` whose mean holding times are `t k = E T_k` (Griffiths & Tavaré 1998, Polanski & Kimmel 2003).
nodes.title: Expected site frequency spectrum under variable population size
